newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oils quiet ahead of PORLA data.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oils quiet ahead of PORLA data.

text.p: European vegetable oil traders were keeping a low profile on Monday as they waited for the Chicago market to settle, and ahead of the PORLA report due for release early on Tuesday morning.

Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wongs latest local output, stocks and exports estimate had little impact on prices as it was within market expectation and release too close to the offical data from PORLA.
"Very few take much notice of the Wong report which is release the day before PORLA's data," said a trader.
Apart for the Tuesday's Malaysian data the only other factor in the market was Chicago's reaction to Friday USDA crop report.
Traders were expecting further falls which were seen in soybeans, but not in the soy oil futures.
However, some were not surprised as many had been talking in terms of an oversold market and were looking for a clear bounce in Chicago sooner rather than later.
"We are getting very close to an oversold market so it has got to bounce soon. But that does not mean Chicago won't go back down," said another trader.
Closing crude palm oil sellers were $7.50 to $5.00 down with no outright business reported although Oct traded at $540 in a switch with Jan/Mar at $525.
Refined palm oil closed around $2.50 lower with no further business reported.
Coconut oil was mixed at $2.50 up to $2.50 down and palmkernel oil unchanged.
Dutch soy oil closed 2.25 guilders down after Oct traded at 89 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
Dutch/EU rape oil finished two to 1.75 guilders lower after Nov/Jan traded at 92.50 and Feb/Apr at 94.50 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill.
